scope.task: Review the authentication/cache boundary and proposed session migration before release

profile_trigger: Cache behavior crosses a current authorization and tenant-isolation boundary.
The proposed migration destructively drops all active session records.
risk_floor.interpretation: The comparison arm is evaluation evidence only; it does not lower the critical floor or authorize a release-routing substitution.

findings.title: A cache hit bypasses current tenant authorization
findings.failure_mode: Service.fetch returns cached content before checking whether the requested tenant is present in the caller's current user['tenants']. Once an authorized request warms a document ID, a caller with no membership can retrieve that content; a user whose membership was revoked can continue retrieving it as well.
affected_inputs: Any request for a cached document_id where tenant is absent from user['tenants'].
Any previously authorized user whose tenant membership is removed after the cache is warmed.
findings.minimal_correction: Move the tenant-membership check ahead of every cache lookup so both misses and hits enforce current membership.

findings.location: service.py:6 and service.py:11 (Service.fetch cache read/write key)
findings.title: The cache key omits tenant identity and leaks the first tenant's document
findings.failure_mode: The cache is indexed only by document_id even though document IDs are not globally unique. The first tenant to warm ID 42 determines the payload returned to every later authorized request for ID 42 in another tenant, producing cross-tenant disclosure and incorrect data.
affected_inputs: Two or more tenants containing the same document_id, after one tenant has warmed that ID.
The second and subsequent tenant requests for that ID, regardless of which tenant warms it first.
findings.minimal_correction: After the mandatory membership check, read and write the cache with key (tenant, document_id), matching the documents key.

findings.title: The session migration drops every active session
findings.failure_mode: migrate_sessions returns an empty list for every input. Any non-empty active-session collection is reduced to zero records, violating the explicit preservation contract and causing total session-state loss for the migrated input.
affected_inputs: Every non-empty input containing one or more active session records.

cases.name: nonempty_active_session_migration
cases.expected: two synthetic active session records with IDs, user IDs, active flags, and claims preserved

findings.minimal_correction: Preserve each active input record one-for-one. For this fixture's unchanged schema, return list(sessions); if a real schema transform is required, copy every active record while retaining identity and all required fields.

smallest_safe_shape: Check `tenant in user['tenants']` before any cache access.
Set `key = (tenant, document_id)` and use key for both cache reads and writes.
Keep the authoritative document lookup keyed by the same tenant/document tuple.
For the fixture contract, return a list containing every input session record.
If the production migration transforms records, assert preservation of every active session ID, required field, and record count before any real migration is authorized.
